MINUTES
  ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE
  APRIL 16, 2019

A regular meeting of the Environmental Advisory Committee was called to order at 7:00 p.m. in
the City Hall Council Chamber, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, by CHAIR ZUCKERMAN.

2.  ROLL CALL

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS PRESENT:  BACINSKI, CHAN-SOUTHWELL,
  LARSON, RADOCCHIO, SCHACHTER,
  STEGURA, UPPAL, ZUCKERMAN

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS ABSENT:  RETZ

  STAFF PRESENT:  ASSISTANT TO THE CITY MANAGER
  DAVIS, ADMINISTRATIVE ASSISTANT
  COREA

3.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

A.  APPROVAL  OF  ENVIRONMENTAL  ADVISORY  COMMITTEE  MEETING
  MINUTES, JANUARY 15, 2019

  COMMITTEE MEMBER STEGURA made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE
  MEMBER LARSON to,

  APPROVE THE ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING
  MINUTES OF JANUARY 15, 2019 AS PRESENTED

  There being no objection, CHAIR ZUCKERMAN so ordered.

4.  AUDIENCE ITEMS WRITTEN/ORAL COMMUNICATIONS NOT ON AGENDA

  NONE

5.  DISCUSSION ITEMS

A.  STORMWATER DISCHARGE COMPLIANCE

CHAIR ZUCKERMAN introduced Kathleen McGowan with Kathleen McGowan Consulting.

Kathleen McGowan provided a presentation with an overview of the City’s Stormwater
Compliance Program, which included examples of the monitoring measures that the City has put
in place.

In response to a question by COMMITTEE MEMBER BACINSKI, Ms. McGowan stated that
Stable Design Guidelines are being developed for new or retrofit stables in the City. The
Environmental Advisory Committee
Meeting Minutes, April 16, 2019
 guidelines will be reviewed by Los Angeles County Department of Building and Safety should be
completed within the next year. CHAIR ZUCKERMAN added that this would not apply to existing
properties with stables and horses.

Assistant to the City Manager Davis stated that she will reach out to the HOA’s and provide them
with the Horse Keeping brochures.

CHAIR ZUCKERMAN stated that there should be more discussion on drought tolerant options as
opposed to discussion on water conservation.

In response to a question by COMMITTEE MEMBER STEGURA, Ms. McGowan confirmed that
a permit is needed for building a barn or for fencing, which would trigger compliance with the
Stable Design Guidelines currently being developed.

COMMITTEE MEMBER STEGURA expressed her concern with the City using herbicide to kill
weeds.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BACINSKI suggested that an incentive program similar to the Clean Bay
program be developed for homeowners.

In response to a concern by COMMITTEE MEMBER UPPAL, Assistant to the City Manager Davis
stated that she will provide more detail regarding a storm drain that failed.

Ms. McGowan provided on overview on how the program is funded. She also encouraged
interested Committee Members to apply for open community seats on the Watershed Area
Steering Committee.

CHAIR ZUCKERMAN stated that the City is currently working on remediation of storm drains.

COMMITTEE MEMBER CHAN-SOUTHWELL asked if the City has a written Stormwater Pollution
Prevention Program. Ms. McGowan stated that the Peninsula Group has an Enhanced Watershed
Management Program. Assistant to the City Manager Davis stated that she will provide the
committee with a link to the document.

Ms. McGowan stated that once comments are received from LA County, a copy of the Stable
Design Guidelines will be provided to the committee.

Assistant to the City Manager Davis stated that staff will provide a link to the Enhanced Watershed
Management Program, work on more outreach to the HOA’s regarding the Manure Program and
drought tolerant options, and provide the Committee feedback on the drainage concerns adjacent
to the golf course.

Ms. McGowan stated that she will confer with her team on the idea of incentives for homeowners.

CHAIR ZUCKERMAN stated that the city’s use of herbicides will be agendized.

Received and filed.

Environmental Advisory Committee
Meeting Minutes, April 16, 2019
 B.  SUSTAINABILITY ELEMENT UPDATE

Assistant to the City Manager David stated that the RFP is in process for the consultant who will
produce the Sustainability Element Update. Information and reports will be provided to the EAC
once available.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BACINSKI requested to view the RFP. Assistant to the City Manager
Davis stated that she will provide it to the committee.

CHAIR ZUCKERMAN provided the committee with a link to the LA County Office of Sustainability
and they will be going through the county’s sustainability plan on May 14th and encouraged the
Committee to attend.

Received and filed.

C.  CLEAN POWER ALLIANCE UPDATE

CHAIR ZUCKERMAN stated that the City Council decided that the businesses will continue at
the lowest tier with the option to opt up. The City will be at the highest tier of 100%.

CHAIR ZUCKERMAN provided the committee with a the CPA Residential Status Report dated
March 26, 2019 showing that the City has one of the lowest opt out rate.

Some commercial have opted up and the city is looking for something to put on their windows for
doing this.

In response to a question Committee Member Bacinski, Assistant to the City Manager Davis
stated that the city has received complaints and is only about 1% to 2% and some of it was
confusion about the program. CHAIR ZUCKERMAN added that there is still an option to opt out.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BACINSKI inquired about the administration cost. CHAIR ZUCKERMAN
stated that he will provide the committee with that information.

COMMITTEE MEMBER STEGURA stated that Sr. Planner Naughton provided a presentation to
the library board and hopes that the library will opt up. Assistant to the City Manager Davis added
that staff is exploring incentives for businesses that opt up per the request of the Committee at its
January meeting.

COMMITTEE MEMBER RADOCCHIO stated that the program launched in February but he was
not able to find the break-out of distribution on the bill. CHAIR ZUCKERMAN stated that he bill
looks the same and may need closer inspection to find. Assistant to the City Manager Davis
referred the Committee to the Clean Power website where a sample bill is available.

Received and filed.

Environmental Advisory Committee
Meeting Minutes, April 16, 2019
 6.  COMMITTEE ITEMS/FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  •  CHAIR ZUCKERMAN stated that at the next meeting the committee could make a
  decision on discussing 5G.

  •  Assistant to the City Manager Davis stated that information on upcoming broadband
  projects will be provided to the committee.

7.  ADJOURNMENT

CHAIR ZUCKERMAN adjourned the meeting at 8:38 p.m.
